content:
melanie_support: Customer (acct: acme-inc) filed an escalation: p99 for long-running streaming calls spiked from ~2s to ~12s over the last 6 hours. They see TTFB unchanged but final completion times blown out.

customer_jennifer: Repro steps we gave: start a chat stream with model=redwood-llama-4, prompt size ~1k tokens, client uses SSE. Observed: first chunk arrives in ~200ms, then final response finishes ~12s later. This breaks UI token-by-token display.

tom_eng: thanks. can you attach a sample trace id? any request ids?

customer_jennifer: trace: trace_id=trc_7fa3c9, request_id=req_fff12. Also see CDN logs showing steady chunk arrival until last chunk stalls.

melanie_support: Adding eng. tagging @tom_eng @charlie_sre. Customer is high priority (SLA).

charlie_sre: quick hypothesis: streaming coalescer / proxy flush window increased or h2 connflow backpressure. TTFB unchanged implies initial flush ok, but mid/final chunks are delayed. Could be KV-cache tail flush or finalization path waiting for buffer timeout.

ivy_prodops: we're seeing a tiny config rollout that changed flush_window default from 20ms -> 200ms for the streaming proxy in region us-west-2 around 2469999000. rolling back now.

incident-bot: deployment 2026-03-15T09:40:10 by ci/cd changed service streaming-proxy config: flush_window_ms=200 (prev=20)

tom_eng: that matches timeline. If proxy increased coalesce window, small trailing chunks will be merged and delayed until the timeout fires. customer severity likely due to many small token chunks at end.

melanie_support: customer confirmed the p95 also moved up on their side, want ETA for rollback and temporary mitigation.

ivy_prodops: rollback started at 2470005480 -> revert applied to streaming-proxy in us-west-2. health checks green.

charlie_sre: can you confirm metrics? checking chunk flush histogram now.

charlie_sre: observed: flush_latency p50=22ms, p95 before rollback=180ms, p99 before rollback=1.1s. After rollback p95=28ms, p99=120ms. Down but still higher than baseline for p99.

tom_eng: follow-ups: 1) investigate client mux behavior (SSE vs h2) 2) check runtime kv-cache finalization path for long-tail blocking 3) instrument final-chunk events with span tags: "final_chunk_wait_reason"

melanie_support: customer asked for a short-term workaround on their side while we confirm. They are on our hosted API.

charlie_sre: short term: 1) we can enable aggressive chunk-flush override for this tenant (flush_window_ms=10) 2) or route their traffic to dedicated pool with bypass coalescer. Both low-risk. Which does customer prefer?

customer_jennifer: route to dedicated pool please. UI team can tolerate small changes. They want minimal dev work.

ivy_prodops: starting tenant routing change to dedicated-tier-02. Should complete in ~3 minutes.

incident-bot: routing change applied for tenant acme-inc -> dedicated-tier-02 at 2470005555

charlie_sre: after route: p99 dropped to ~200ms for end-to-end on a replay. Looks good. We'll keep routing for 24h and monitor.

melanie_support: Communicated to customer. They ran a few sessions and reported UX fixed.

customer_jennifer: confirming: a few sample calls now complete ~250ms p99. Thanks.

tom_eng: next steps for long-term: revert the accidental config change and add a canary gating rule so flush_window changes require perf-sanity check. Also add an alert for flush_window drift per region.

charlie_sre: dev work: instrument final chunk path and add metric "final_chunk_wait_ms" with labels {region, tenant, flush_window_ms, mux_protocol}. Add trace annotation when wait > 100ms.

ivy_prodops: ops work: add config-guard webhook to ci/cd to block flush_window > 50ms without manual approval. Also add a playbook entry for tenant routing during streaming latency regressions.

melanie_support: I'll send a summary + RCA to the customer and mark incident resolved after 24h of observations. Will include repro steps we used and how to request routing.

tom_eng: quick repro script for internal use (curl SSE):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-llama-4" \ 
  -d '{"messages": [{"role":"user","content":"'"$(python - <<'PY'\nprint('x'*1000)\nPY)"'"'}]}'
```

charlie_sre: add note: when reproducing, test with both SSE and http2 streaming client; h2 connection-window and envoy downstream flow control can hide coalescing issues differently.

melanie_support: logged follow-up tasks: ENG-2042 (instrument final_chunk_wait), OPS-1109 (config-guard webhook), SRE-3078 (streaming routing playbook).

customer_jennifer: appreciated. we'll keep you posted if anything else pops up. thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

melanie_support: closing loop for now. keeping thread open until 2470082000 for final 24h validation.

charlie_sre: leaving a pointer: potential root cause chain = accidental config rollout -> increased coalesce timeout -> trailing token accumulation -> final-chunk wait -> UI-visible p99 spike. Preventable with canary + metric alert.

melanie_support: thanks everyone.
